newsitem.title: UK: FX in Europe - Dlr regains poise after stock scare.
newsitem.headline: FX in Europe - Dlr regains poise after stock scare.

text.p: The dollar stabilised against the mark on Monday, recovering sharp early losses in Europe as concerns about a second day of turbulence on global stock markets proved unfounded.

Friday's 3.1 percent drop in the Dow Jones Industrial Average of leading U.S. stocks raised fears of panic selling on the world's bourses this week and talk of a further slide on Wall Street accelerated the dollar retreat in early trade.
The spectre of a crash eased quickly on Monday, however, as European markets quickly pared losses, the Dow opened higher and the dollar bounced from supports about 1.8050 marks.

"The dollar was being priced straight off Wall Street today and when steadier European markets began pointing to a Dow recovery, the dollar followed suit," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas in London.
Parsons said the whether the Dow can sustain its early gains will still be important for the dollar. But he said important chart support levels had held and medium-term uptrends remained intact.
At 1501 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.8220/25 marks compared with 1.8210/20 in late European trade on Friday. The Dow was up 14.4 points, or 0.18 percent.
Analysts said the minor panic in the dollar and Dow late Friday was exaggerated by thin, holiday-affected markets and there was little fresh incentive for follow-up selling Monday.
This was especially so as traders await the outcome this week of the key policy-making meetings at the U.S. Federal Reserve and the German Bundesbank.

While few analysts expect the Fed's Open Market Committee to change its interest rates on Tuesday, there is still some lingering speculation the Bundesbank may move to tighten credit when its central council meets on Thursday.
This buoyed the mark across the board over the past week.
Yet, ironically, the recovery of the mark on rate rise speculation has caused that speculation to ease, analysts said.
"The recovery of the mark has been a sort of self-correcting mechanism," said Parsons at Paribas.

"The Bundesbank strategy in defence of the mark has been to foster the impression that the next move in rates is up without having to deliver it (a rate rise). The problem is that one or the other may eventually have to give way."
On balance analysts do not now expect a rise in German rates this week, but there is still a debate about a reversion to a variable rate securities repurchase tender on Tuesday.
Allowing the market to set the weekly repo rate could see that key market rate rise by a basis point or two from the current 3.0 percent fixed rate.
But analysts see policy basically unchanged.

"Now that there seems to be some calming down of those pressures (mark weaknesss), I think the Bundesbank is happy not to do anything," Deustche Bank chief economist Norbert Walter told Reuters Financial Television.
The mark is more than one percent higher against a trade-weighted basket of global currencies over the past 10 trading days.
Elsewhere, sterling/mark tracked dollar/mark's recovery and the pound also gleaned some independent support against the dollar following positive UK budget data for July.
The UK government repaid a bigger-than-expected 3.875 billion sterling of public debt in July, with Value Added Tax receipts at their highest level ever during the month.
Analysts said this underlines the buoyancy of the domestic economy and should buoy sterling.
Dollar/yen was firmer on the steadier Dow and on relief Japan's July trade surplus was not as big as feared.
--Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
